name: 5,6-methylenedioxy-N-methyl-2-aminoindane
summary: MDMAI, also known as 5,6-methylenedioxy-N-methyl-2-aminoindane, is a drug of the 2-aminoindane family developed in the 1990s by a team led by David E. Nichols at Purdue University. It acts as a non-neurotoxic serotonin releasing agent (SRA) in animals and is a putative entactogen in humans.
